news.title: Niemann wins as Rahm secures LIV season title
news.text:
Joaquin Niemann led throughout to win the LIV Golf New York event on Sunday, while Jon Rahm secured his third straight season title.

Niemann fired a two-under 69 to finish on 16 under after 72 holes at Trump National Bedminster in New Jersey.

That meant the Chilean won by three strokes from American Harold Varner III and the 27-year-old met US President Donald Trump after extending his record for LIV wins to nine.

“I feel like the more they push me, the better golfer I’m going to become from every experience,” said Niemann.

England’s Lee Westwood and Scott Vincent of Zimbabwe were both seven off the pace in a share for third place.

Rahm finished tied for 41st after closing with a round of 76, but the Spaniard has clinched the season title.

The world number 13 has an unassailable 219-point lead over American Bryson DeChambeau heading into the final individual event of the season at Indianapolis in two weeks.

The 31-year-old won last year’s season title despite not winning a single event, but this year has two wins from 12 so far – in Hong Kong and Mexico – and has also had four runner-up finishes.

news.title: Questions I Have After Learning That Trump Was Allegedly Smuggled Out of Air Force One in a Catering Box
news.text:
We already knew something weird happened with Donald Trump last month in Turkey, even by the already weird standards of this administration. He ordered new military strikes against Iran while in Turkey for a NATO summit—meaning he was unusually close to the fireworks he was creating. Then, when he left Turkey for the U.K., the official story was cagey and self-contradictory, and involved him supposedly flying on an older Air Force One-designated plane, instead of his brand new, more luxurious Air Force One.

However, it’s now being reported that the president flew to the U.K. not on the new Air Force One nor one of the Old Air Force Ones, but that he got on one of the old planes and posed for the press like everything was normal, and then slipped out a cargo door and into a catering box, which got carted off to a military plane, which he then flew aboard all the way to the U.K.

The Washington Post first reported this on Monday, and the New York Times corroborated it on Tuesday. Yes, Trump was apparently conveyed in a dang food container according to credible reporting. In video footage published by the Times, the box had the logo of Austrian catering company Do & Co on it, and was detached and lowered onto a truck with a scissor lift, as is common with such containers according to the official Do & Co website.

 Video shows the airport catering truck used in a secret operation to move President Trump from Air Force One to another U.S. government plane amid a credible Iranian threat last month. The truck can be seen pulling away from Air Force One after the president had boarded the… pic.twitter.com/IwJTaWlmSb — CBS News (@CBSNews) August 11, 2026

Before the report about the catering box, I had recently written about Trump’s new, Qatar-gifted Air Force One. Even though the defensive capabilities of Air Force One are top secret, aviation aficionados are fairly certain the new plane was not beefed up with the sort of anti-missile capabilities the president’s older planes had boasted. For Trump to scurry off to the relatively safety of an older plane as soon as Iran posed a potential threat made sense as far as I was concerned.

But in light of what we now know, this story does not fully make sense when you dig into the details, and as such I have some questions:

What was supposed to happen to the people on Air Force One if Iran attacked it?

Out of many Veep-like aspects to this story, perhaps the Veepiest is this: according to the New York Times, there were reporters and White House staffers on the older Air Force One plane that day, and they allegedly believed Trump was actually onboard when it took off. This, the Times says, was part of the “ruse,” and the people on the plane were there “to serve as unknowing decoys.” The BBC reported at the time that passengers were asked to keep the window shades closed during the flight.

To spell this out a little bit more, if the Times’ reporting is accurate, the ruse could have involved smuggling Trump out of the plane, and then keeping it stationary on the runway—say, due to some fake technical difficulties—while Trump secretly slipped into the U.K., and then announced the switcheroo immediately after he landed. Instead, amid what was reportedly a credible—and presumably mortal—threat, am I to understand that his administration decided to have a plane full of suckers take off and fly almost 2,000 miles across Europe with, essentially, a big “Donald Trump is inside this plane” sign on it?

Why was the Trump Administration so unbelievably cagey when they were allegedly sneaking around?

Even at the time, this move was confusing in part because it seemed like the administration was jerking the public around. Trump himself said he was flying on the obsolete plane “for old time’s sake.” However, when he switched back to Air Force One—the new one—at Mildenhall Air Force Base in the U.K., he posted on Truth Social that the brave heroes over at Mildenhall “should be the first” to see the new Air Force One.

 “To honor our brave men and women of the Military, we are sending the brand new, and truly spectacular, Air Force One to Mildenhall Air Force Base, in the United Kingdom, to give them a chance to tour the Aircraft…” – President Donald J. Trump 🇺🇸 pic.twitter.com/Nf2qCGDKUs — The White House (@WhiteHouse) July 8, 2026

With no disrespect whatsoever intended for the military personnel at Mildenhall Air Force Base, which is actually a U.K. air force installation that the U.S. and NATO use for refueling, there are a lot of US Air Force bases in Europe—including one very big and important one, Ramstein—so why in the world would these specific people either care, or deserve any such privilege?

But that’s just one weird hole in the official story from last month, because…

Wait. Why was the official story that he switched planes at all?

In the newly reported sequence of events, Trump’s secret military plane allegedly landed in Mildenhall separately from the old Air Force One plane. Trump was then allegedly smuggled into that Air Force One, and then photographed leaving it, only to eventually depart from Mildenhall in plane number 3: his new, Qatar-gifted Air Force One. That plan has a ton of moving parts! The most sense I can make of it is that the Trump Administration was hoping to discourage Iran from attempting a missile strike by pretending the president was aboard the more defensively robust, older plane.

But keep in mind that Trump has claimed that the new Air Force One is “considered ​the world’s most luxurious plane,” and said, “When it was built, it was built at a level that will probably never be seen again.” Even if he weren’t in it, would Donald Trump, who once lived in the world’s gaudiest apartment, be willing to risk letting Iran blow up such a plane? Better, perhaps, to pretend to be on a less luxurious plane, and get that one blown up instead.

Did the Trump Administration announce its alleged trick immediately without anyone noticing?

In response to questions from the New York Times about the plane swap back on July 8, Trump’s communications director, Steven Cheung, gave statements that sounded downright idiotic when all anyone thought had happened was that the president had switched to an older plane. Here’s what the Times published, emphasis Gizmodo’s:

 “[T]he new Air Force One is a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the president and his staff. “[…] As the president has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal — including distraction and misdirection — to address those threats.”

In the moment, the “misdirection” Cheung was referring to was, supposedly, the masterful gambit of getting on one plane rather than another. Assuming these reports are true, was Cheung’s statement terrible op-sec, or—if you want to be maximally generous—was Cheung dropping hints like a comic book villain?

Gizmodo asked the White House for confirmation of the Times and the Post’s reporting, and to comment on these matters, but did not receive an immediate reply.
news.author: Mike Pearl

news.title: South Carolina polls close as Republicans select candidate for Lindsey Graham's Senate seat
news.text:
WASHINGTON – Polls in South Carolina closed on Aug 11 in the Republican vote to decide if Darline Graham will replace her late brother, Senator Lindsey Graham, as the Republican nominee for US Senate in November’s election, following his death in July.

Governor Henry McMaster had appointed Darline Graham to serve the rest of the senator’s term through early January, after his unexpected death from a heart ailment.

President Donald Trump endorsed Darline Graham, who has never held public office, for a full six-year term, calling it a “fabulous tribute” to her brother.

But critics said her bid, based on family name recognition and presidential backing without a political record of her own, had the air of an attempted coronation. Ten candidates stood for the Republican nomination in the election on Aug 11. If none of them wins a majority on Aug 11, the top two finishers will head to an Aug 25 runoff.

The winner will face Democrat Annie Andrews, a paediatrician who had more than $3 million (S$3.84 million) in her campaign war chest at the start of July.

Graham’s opponents include US Representatives Ralph Norman and Russell Fry, former Governor Mark Sanford and self-funded Greenville businessman Mark Lynch.

Alabama vote in redrawn seat

In nearby Alabama, Republicans in the state’s 2nd Congressional District for the US House were deciding who will be their candidate in a seat that they hope to flip from the Democrats with help from a redrawn map.

The race is potentially crucial to their bid to hold the House, which they narrowly control.

The Republican majorities in Congress are essential to Trump’s ability to power ahead with his agenda, but he faces a tough challenge ahead in the November midterm election, given a low approval rating that has eroded further as the Iran war drags on and gasoline prices remain high.

Republican-led states in the US South rushed through a round of congressional redistricting earlier in 2026, to take advantage of an April Supreme Court decision that severely weakened the Voting Rights Act, a 1965 law intended to prevent discrimination in voting.

Earlier in 2026, the court cleared the way for Alabama to use a congressional map that favours Republicans by eliminating one of two districts where Black voters make up a majority or near-majority. Polls in Alabama close at 7pm (8am Wednesday Singapore time) and the Republican winner will face incumbent Democrat Shomari Figures, who is Black and is hoping for a second term.

Time for change in South Carolina?

Lindsey Graham won his June 9 primary in South Carolina by almost 28 percentage points, as he sought his fifth Senate term. Lynch, who placed second with nearly 29 per cent of the vote, is the only candidate in the special primary from the original primary field.

Lynch received more than 130,000 votes in that primary, suggesting some Republican primary voters had an appetite for change before Lindsey Graham’s death.

news.title: Just 29% of expected midterm voters say they approve of Trump’s handling of Iran
news.text:
A cable TV polling expert claims that numbers from two surveys conducted two years apart show just how deeply President Donald Trump has disappointed America's voters when it comes to Iran.

CNN chief data analyst Harry Enten said Tuesday that a July 2024 poll of people who were extremely motivated to vote in that year’s presidential election found that 53 percent were confident Trump would be able to handle the situation in Iran, according to a video clip posted online.

But a July poll of people extremely motivated to vote in November's midterm elections shows that just 29 percent now approve of how Trump is actually handling Iran, Enten said.

"We're talking about a 24-point fall in just two years," he said. "What was an advantage for President Trump going into the 2024 election amongst those who really wanted to turn out and vote has turned into a tremendous disadvantage this time around."

Enten added: "Promises were made and promises were not kept. They were broken as far as those voters were concerned."

In a prepared statement, White House spokesperson David Ingle told The Independent, "What matters most to the American people is having a Commander-in-Chief who takes decisive action to eliminate threats and keep them safe, which is exactly what President Trump is doing."

"The President does not make these incredibly important national security decisions based on fluid opinion polls or political pundits, but on the best interests of the American people," he added.

It's been more than five months since Trump started his war against Iran on February 28, without congressional approval, leading to 18 U.S. military deaths and the closing of the Strait of Hormuz, which increased global oil prices.

The newly-named secretary of Iran's National Security Council, Moshen Rezaei, vowed Tuesday that the strait would remain closed until the U.S. ends the war, releases frozen Iranian assets and stops all conflicts in the region, "including in Lebanon and Gaza," according to Reuters.

Rezaei announced the demands one day after Trump said that he wanted Iran to pay compensation for all of "the damage ​they've done over a 50-year period," and that he was considering letting Iran's economy collapse or hitting the country "really, really hard."

Polling on which political party is more trusted to deal with wars, conflicts and terrorism also spells trouble for Republicans, who were ahead of Democrats by 18 percentage points in January 2025, Enten said.

"That advantage, because of President Trump, has turned into a disadvantage on a core, key question that almost always favors Republicans. Now, Democrats have a two-point edge," he said.

Enten also said that "perhaps the most shocking thing" was the question of whether the U.S. would "ultimately reach a good deal with Iran."

"Just 27 percent of all voters believe that, and get this: just 41 percent of Republicans believe it," he said. "We are seeing below 50 percent across the board on this issue, and this is the reason I think, more than any other, that folks disagree with Trump on Iran because they, simply put, don't see what the point of it is. They don't see a way out of it."

As of Tuesday, the Real Clear Polling website gave Democrats an average edge of 7.1 percentage points over Republicans in a generic congressional contest, 48.6-41.5.

news.title: North Korea fires second missile in a week ahead of South Korea-US drills
news.text: North Korea on Wednesday carried out its second ballistic missile test in less than a week, according to South Korea and Japan, in a move seen as a likely protest against upcoming South Korea-US military drills that Pyongyang describes as a rehearsal for invasion.The launch came two days after Seoul and Washington said they would begin their annual large-scale Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises on August 17 to strengthen readiness against North Korean threats. Multiple UN Security Council resolutions ban North Korea from launching ballistic missiles, but Pyongyang has continued to expand its missile and nuclear programmes.South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said a ballistic missile was fired from the eastern coastal area of Wonsan at about 6 am and flew more than 700 km. It said South Korea remained ready to repel any provocation by North Korea in coordination with the United States. South Korea's presidential National Security Council also urged the North to stop ballistic missile launches, calling them "acts of provocation" that defy UN Security Council resolutions.Japan's Defence Ministry said it had also detected what it believed was a ballistic missile launch from North Korea. It said the weapon was not seen reaching Japan's exclusive economic zone, suggesting it fell farther away from the Japanese coast.North Korea has often reacted to Ulchi Freedom Shield and other major South Korea-US military exercises with weapons tests and strong statements, while Seoul and Washington have repeatedly said the drills are defensive. After last year's Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises began, North Korean leader Kim Jong Un said the drills showed the US and South Korea's "will to ignite a war" and claimed they had become more provocative than before, prompting North Korea to take "proactive and overwhelming" countermeasures.On August 6, South Korea, the US and Japan detected the launch of a short-range ballistic missile from North Korea in what was its first ballistic weapons test since late June. North Korea did not confirm that reported launch, though it usually releases details of weapons tests a day later. The country has increased ballistic and other weapons testing since Kim's high-stakes diplomacy with US President Donald Trump collapsed in 2019. Experts say Kim is likely trying to use his expanded arsenal to win concessions from the US, including relief from international economic sanctions. In recent years, Kim has also widened North Korea's diplomatic outreach by deepening ties with Russia, including supplying troops and ammunition for its war in Ukraine, and by taking steps to strengthen relations with China. Chinese President Xi Jinping visited Pyongyang in June for the first time in seven years.Wednesday's launch, the second in under a week, came as South Korea and the US prepared for fresh joint military drills, underlining a familiar pattern of North Korean missile activity, regional condemnation and renewed focus on Pyongyang's growing weapons programme.With PTI Inputs- EndsPublished By: India Today Web Desk Published On: Aug 12, 2026 06:10 IST

news.title: Tottenham Hotspur’s Daniel Levy said to have missed share issue deadline
news.text:
Tottenham Hotspur, the English Premier League football team owned by the Lewis family, has told minority shareholder and former chairman Daniel Levy that he missed the deadline to participate in a team share issue.

The club recently raised money through the issue of new shares in ENIC Sports, a holding company that has a controlling interest in Tottenham. The Lewis family announced it had invested £100 million in the shares and had offered Levy the opportunity to participate in accordance with his stake.

Levy first requested an extension to the timetable, said a person close to the Lewis family who asked not to be identified because the information was private.He then committed to funding and was given 10 further days to fund, the person said.

The person said Levy has not funded and the deadline has passed, meaning that his stake in ENIC will be diluted from its current level of around 29 per cent.

That means that Tottenham, which narrowly avoided relegation from the Premier League last season, will lose out on a further contribution from Levy. But the club has received around £200 million from the Lewis family since September. The Lewis family declined to comment. Levy did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Tottenham, despite performing poorly last season, is still one of the most valuable teams in England. Its revenues have been boosted by a modern stadium that also hosts National Football League games, boxing matches and concerts.

Amid clashes involving billionaire Joe Lewis and his family, Levy left his role as executive chairman of the club in September after nearly 25 years in charge. Levy and Lewis had been in business for decades through an investment trust initially known as English National Investment Co., or ENIC. The pair acquired stakes in several European clubs, including Tottenham in 2001.

While Levy’s focus remained largely on the club, Lewis continued to build his fortune through the Tavistock Group, which he founded.Lewis and his family are now worth about US$9.6 billion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

In 2022, Lewis relinquished control of Tottenham, transferring his majority stake in ENIC to the Lewis Family Trust. In 2024, he pleaded guilty to US charges of insider trading and securities fraud and was pardoned the following year by US President Donald Trump. BLOOMBERG

news.title: Raskin Demands Answers From Justice, Interior After Reflecting Pool Reversal
news.text:
The ranking Democratic member of the House Judiciary Committee announced an investigation into key members of the Trump administration Tuesday for bringing “baseless” charges against a former Olympian canoeist over alleged vandalism of the National Mall’s Reflecting Pool.

The announcement was accompanied by the public release of a letter that Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.) wrote to Jeanine Pirro, U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia, and Doug Burgum, secretary of the U.S. Department of the Interior.

The letter framed the issue by saying that at the end of July, the U.S. Justice Department “admitted it had baselessly indicted and prosecuted an innocent American citizen based on trumped-up charges of ‘vandalizing’ the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.”

That citizen was David Hearn, one of Raskin’s constituents from his Maryland district that abuts the District of Columbia.

Hearn, 67, is a former canoeist for the U.S. Olympic team. He navigated the Reflecting Pool in the past, legally, as a way of promoting the sport during the U.S. bicentennial celebration in 1976.

The former Olympian canoeist was arrested where he had once dipped his paddle into the water on June 19, for actions whose full extent is disputed.

Hearn and his legal team maintain that he was looking into the Reflecting Pool, saw something weird, reached into the water to examine a section that was coming up, and was arrested by the United States Park Police, assisted by the National Guard, for it.

The charge that the U.S. Department of Justice attempted to bring against him was a felony count of destruction of public property worth more than $1,000, which could have put him in jail for up to 10 years.

In a pair of President Donald Trump’s posts on Truth Social that the White House directed The Epoch Times to, published on Aug. 7 and 9, Trump painted Hearn’s actions as part of a broader effort to vandalize the Reflecting Pool and publicly asked Pirro to reconsider her decision not to prosecute.

“A National Park Service career employee, a highly credible witness, saw David Hearn (ActBlue) in broad daylight vandalize the Reflecting Pool by ‘violently’ ripping and tugging at the Pool’s somewhat delicate coating,” Trump wrote.

ActBlue is a progressive Democratic political action committee to which Hearn may have given some small donations. “David Hearn” is a common name that shows up for many different people as donors to that organization in the Federal Election Commission’s database.

The pool’s “somewhat delicate coating” that the president referred to is also a matter of dispute related to the pool coating’s deterioration and an accompanying algae bloom.

Trump is making the case that the re-coating of the pool in the dark blue of the American flag might have worked out but for sabotage.

Many Democrats believe that story is largely false and is being used as a cover for a botched $15 million contracting job. It appears that Pirro was leaning in their direction, having moved to dismiss the charges against Hearn.

Raskin has questions about how one of his constituents faced the possibility of a decade behind bars for this.

The congressman is demanding a slew of documents from the Departments of Justice and the Interior by Aug. 25. These include all documents on the decision to prosecute Hearn, all Hearn-related communications between the DOJ, DOI, and the White House, and all evidence presented before a grand jury against Hearn.

Raskin’s office did not immediately reply to a request for comment about whether some sanction would have been appropriate for Hearn, if he would be working to claw back some of the $15 million awarded to re-coat the Reflecting Pool, and what he thought of the president’s call for the U.S. attorney for Washington, D.C., to launch a renewed prosecution.
news.author: Jeremy Lott

news.title: Race To Replace Lindsey Graham Heading To Runoff
news.text:
President Donald Trump was unable to clear the field Tuesday for his choice to replace Sen. Lindsey Graham when the late South Carolina Republican’s younger sister, Darline Graham, failed to win a clear majority in the GOP primary election.

Graham, a 62-year-old vocational rehabilitation administrator, by mid-Tuesday evening, is certain to make the Aug. 25 runoff and will face one of two congressmen battling for the number two spot, either Russell Fry or Ralph Norman. The winner of that race will face pediatrician Annie Andrews, who won the Democratic nomination in June, in the November general election.

Graham’s elder brother won the GOP nomination in June as he sought his fifth term in the Senate, but died on July 11 of an aortic dissection — a tear in the main artery from his heart — brought on by heart disease.

Unlike Lindsey Graham, whose political career began 34 years ago with a run for a South Carolina state legislative seat, Darline Graham’s career began exactly four weeks ago, two days after her brother’s death. While she was first discussed as a caretaker for the position until the new Congress starts in January, Trump quickly pushed for her to run for the full six-year term.

news.title: Trump Air Force One deception under scrutiny after passengers allegedly used as ‘decoy’
news.text:
Democrats are demanding a congressional briefing after US President Donald Trump was secretly moved from Air Force One to another aircraft amid an alleged Iranian threat, while reporters and White House staff remained on the presidential plane.

The operation, first reported by the Washington Post and also detailed by the New York Times, took place during Trump's return from a Nato summit last month.

Trump reportedly boarded Air Force One before secretly leaving through a side door and transferring to an Air Force C-32A. 

More than 100 aides, officials and journalists remained aboard the original aircraft without being told about the alleged threat.

Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal told CNN the operation was “unprecedented and surreal” and “downright scary”.

“I want to know what precautions were taken to make sure that all of the passengers on that Air Force One, which was judged too dangerous for the president to fly on, what precautions were taken to keep the staff and reporters on that plane safe?” he said.

The White House has not confirmed details of the operation. Communications director Steven Cheung told the Washington Post that officials used “every tool at our disposal” to protect Trump.

Trump later appeared to acknowledge security concerns when asked why reporters had been ordered to close their window shades.

“You’re probably on a dangerous flight. But if I go, you go. Right?” Trump said.

news.title: California US senator pushes for nationwide legal representation for immigrants
news.text:
A California U.S. senator wants to ensure that anyone in the nation facing potential deportation is entitled to legal representation

Last week, U.S. Sen. Adam Schiff re-introduced federal legislation that would guarantee the right to legal representation for all people in deportation or legal immigration proceedings if they are unable to afford it. Similar bills have been put forth in years past, but the legislation now has added importance under President Donald Trump’s mass deportation campaign.

Research consistently finds that legal representation is crucial to improving an individual’s chances of applying for relief and winning their immigration case. Immigrants with legal counsel were 5.5 times more likely to obtain relief from deportation, according to one UCLA School of Law study.

“President Trump’s cruel immigration agenda has caused unimaginable, long-lasting harm in our communities, leading to unlawful deportations that have torn thousands of families apart,” Schiff said in a statement. “Having access to legal counsel during immigration proceedings is essential to fair outcomes, yet beyond the reach of many.”

Identical legislation to Schiff’s has been introduced in the U.S. House by Rep. Norma Torres, D-Pomona, who has led previous efforts to establish “universal representation” for immigrants. Legal representation in fiscal year 2026 immigration court proceedings is at the lowest level since 2010, according to Austin Kocher, a research professor at Syracuse University who analyzes immigration data.

“Access to legal representation is easily one of the most important factors in whether immigrants facing deportation get a fair hearing,” Kocher said in a statement.

Schiff’s bill would establish an Office of Immigration Representation and provide counsel for immigrants in several types of situations including bond hearings, state court proceedings and those seeking temporary protected status.

The legislation follows a similar statewide attempt proposed by Assemblymember Mia Bonta, D-Alameda, earlier this year. AB 2600 would create a program to provide legal counsel to Californians facing deportation proceedings and give priority to people held in detention facilities.

Last year, Gov. Gavin Newsom signed a law also authored by Bonta that expanded access to legal representation for immigrant youth.

news.title: Trump walks in to sparklers and does YMCA dance at controversial Patriot Games final in Ohio
news.text:
President Trump made a brief appearance on Tuesday at the finals of the Patriot Games, the three-day teen athletics tournament his administration helped organize as part of America’s 250th anniversary celebrations.

The administration was likely hoping for a better turnout than its Great American State Fair, which suffered widespread mockery online and poor attendance.

The Republican arrived Tuesday evening on a rainy day in Cleveland to take in the competition, which was being held at the SPIRE Academy sports boarding school, where organizers reportedly again struggled to fill seats.

He entered the arena in a shower of sparklers alongside ESPN’s Pat McAfee, leading a group of competitors who had battled against delegations representing all 50 states and various U.S. territories and tribal nations to make it to the final.

For a Donald Trump production, the president was relatively muted, giving a brief interview with ESPN’s Laura Rutledge about how he was “very proud” of the athletes and parents in the room while praising their “love for our country.” Naturally, he also did his signature shimmy dance move as confetti fell on the winners.

The upbeat atmosphere masked some of the questions that have swirled around the event.

Student athletes, who won entrance to the games based on patriotic video submissions rather than qualifying competition, told The Washington Post they were unnerved to see those chosen to compete were almost entirely white, despite the country’s wide diversity. 

“It’s a little startling,” one player said. “This is supposed to be the best high school athletes. … It just feels a little concerning not to see very many different types of people.”

Other critics noted multiple states had non-residents representing them.

Though the president didn’t appear to comment on it at the games, another key thread was gender and athletics.

The White House has cracked down on federally supported schools that allow transgender people to compete in leagues matching their gender identity, and the president pledged last year that “there will be no men playing in women’s sports” at the games.

For their part, many of the student competitors seemed to be enjoying themselves, chanting “USA!” and cheering the president during the finals.
news.summary: The president got a rockstar welcome at the Ohio tournament, even as questions hovered around its selection process

news.title: Darline Graham Advances to GOP Senate Runoff in South Carolina
news.text:
GREENVILLE, S.C.—The special Republican primary election to replace the late Lindsey Graham as South Carolina’s Senate nominee has narrowed.

Graham’s sister, current Sen. Darline Graham (R-S.C.) will advance to an August 25 runoff.

Reps. Russell Fry (R-S.C.) and Ralph Norman (R-S.C.) are vying for second.

The Associated Press made the call after 8:10 p.m., more than an hour after the polls closed.

As of 8:26 p.m., with an approximate 48 percent of the vote counted, she had 32.8 percent of the vote to 23.3 Norman and 22.3 for Fry.

The winner of the Republican contest faces the Democratic nominee, Dr. Annie Andrews, in November.

The current senator, a newcomer to electoral politics, replaced her brother in the upper chamber with the support of President Donald Trump, who has also endorsed her campaign for the nomination.

Fry entered the race after Trump suggested during a Newsmax interview that the congressman entering that race “could happen.” He said Fry was “a very, very talented person.”

Norman, who endorsed former South Carolina Gov. Nikki Haley against Trump in 2024, has been backed by figures aligned with the conservative Freedom Caucus.

In addition to Darline Graham, Norman, and Fry, the hopefuls included former South Carolina Gov. Mark Sanford, businessman Mark Lynch, farmer Danny Lee Ford, retiree Glenda Gail Parker, engineer and scientist Samuel Shepherd, lawyer Duke Buckner, and former Myrtle Beach Mayor Mark McBride.

Polling ahead of the race did not show a clear frontrunner, though Darline Graham, Norman, and Fry have generally traded the top three spots.

The race quickly attracted big money and attention.

Backers of Fry and Darline Graham dominated ad spending in the race, with $1.5 million and $1.4 million in support, respectively, according to an Aug. 7 analysis from AdImpact. Sanford followed with $866,000, while Lynch and Norman fell third and fourth, garnering $233,000 and $231,000 in that spending, respectively.

Darline Graham also received support from the National Republican Senatorial Committee, a key hub for GOP fundraising.

Recent campaign finance reports show that her campaign quickly raised hundreds of thousands of dollars.

The Sanford and Lynch campaigns led Fry and Norman when it came to cash on hand. While the former governor and businessman had roughly $1.3 million and $547,000 as of late July, at that same period, the two members of Congress had about $485,000 and $171,000, respectively.

From Greenville to Rock Hill, polling places across northern South Carolina appeared sleepy much of Aug. 11.

South Carolinians there and elsewhere in the state were reluctant to stop and talk about the race.

One reason may have been the high humidity and blazing heat. A digital sign outside the First Baptist North Spartanburg read more than 96 degrees Fahrenheit.

Outside that Spartanburg polling place, Chuck Robbins told The Epoch Times his top issues were border security and “economics overall,” including affordability.

While many candidates have pledged to tackle those concerns, Sanford was the man who earned his vote.

“I just don’t think she has the experience that we need,” he said of Darline Graham, adding that he liked the job her late brother had done in Washington.

South Carolinians had a chance to compare Sanford and other leading hopefuls during an early August debate. In the days ahead of Election Day, multiple candidates made their pitches to voters in interviews with The Epoch Times.

Norman told The Epoch Times and others on Aug. 10 that he would work with Sens. Rick Scott (R-Fla.) and Mike Lee (R-Utah) to force a talking filibuster to advance the SAVE America Act, election integrity legislation that would boost citizenship verification requirements for voter registration and require photo ID to vote.

The real estate developer and fiscal conservative, known for forcing intra-Republican debates on the cost of party-line bills, warned of the scope of the national debt, describing it as “the cancer that’s killing us.”

Norman also drew attention to the threat from the Chinese Communist Party, noting that he had worked to close Chinese-affiliated Confucius Institutes in the United States.

“How long are we going to be stooges?” he asked.

In Greenville, the home to his family’s longstanding appliance store and showroom, Lynch stressed his business background.

“I have a servant’s heart. We’ve served customers every day, and we’ve got a great reputation here,” Lynch told The Epoch Times.

He’s concerned about the spread of Islam in South Carolina, voicing opposition to the small, all-Muslim community of Holy Islamville, located in York County.

That view and others, including his concern with the impact of illegal aliens on the economy, are part of why he wants the United States to end the Iran War.

“We’ve got problems here at home,” he said.

Shepherd, in an email interview with The Epoch Times, also emphasized his private sector experience—in his case, as a biomedical engineer.

“I bring the same engineering mindset to the Senate: Identify the root problem, cut waste, measure outcomes, and fix what is broken,” he said.

Like Norman, he warned of the scale of the U.S. debt, vowing to oppose any bill that raises the deficit.

He also said he would seek to safeguard Medicare and Social Security, two large programs that are widely used by Americans but also help to drive the growth of the national debt.
news.author: Nathan Worcester
